newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia seeks foreign help against crime ring.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia seeks foreign help against crime ring.

text.p: Nineteen of 81 ethnic Chinese alleged to be part of an international crime syndicate were questioned in court on Thursday as a top Cambodian police official appealed for international assistance in the case.
"This organisation is not small. This is a syndicate of criminals," Police General Skadavy M. Ly Roun said in an interview with Reuters.
"We have limited means, and we need international cooperation," he said, adding that he had talked with French and Chinese authorities about the case and will meet U.S. officials soon.

Colonel Lam Buntha, deputy chief of Cambodia's Interpol office, an agency funded by the Interior Ministry and separate from police, told Reuters the court was questioning the men to determine how to handle their cases.
Lam Buntha said he did not expect any decision from the court until Friday because questioning, being done individually, was slowed by a lack of interpreters.

The 19 Chinese being quizzed on Thursday have no passports. They have been detained since Christmas Day when a raid on a Phnom Penh villa turned up 81 Chinese believed to be involved in an international crime syndicate.
The passports of the others in detention are being investigated since some had pictures that did not match their bearers.
All 81 were being held at the police immigration detention centre except for three alleged ringleaders who were in custody at Cambodia's Interpol, Skadavy said.

At the villa, police found fake Chinese and Cambodian immigration stamps, 26 fake Chinese passports, a phone book listing suspected criminal contacts in Europe, South America, the United States and Africa, and a small amount of amphetamines, Skadavy said.
Interpol officials said the Chinese were being held on three charges: making fake passports, human trafficking and illegal drug use.
